cases.expected_note: Microsoft publishes =SUMXMY2({2, 3, 9, 1, 8, 7, 5}, {6, 5, 11, 7, 5, 4, 4}) = 79, matching the range row.

cases.description: Arrays of different lengths, which the page assigns an error code
cases.expected_note: The Remarks publish: "If array_x and array_y do not have the same number of values, SUMXMY2 returns the #N/A error value."

cases.description: Squaring the difference makes the function symmetric in its two arguments
cases.expected_note: (x-y)^2 = (y-x)^2, so SUMXMY2 must be symmetric while SUMX2MY2 must ANTI-symmetric. A structural assertion with no derived constant, and the one that most sharply separates the two names: the same swap applied to SUMX2MY2 would give -88 - 88 = -176, not 0.

cases.description: The definition checked against the engine's own SUMPRODUCT over an array expression
cases.expected_note: SUMXMY2(x,y) = SUMPRODUCT((x-y)^2) by definition. No constant from us. This case also exercises array arithmetic inside SUMPRODUCT, so a #VALUE! here would point at the array handling rather than at SUMXMY2 -- worth reading alongside the two simpler cases above before concluding anything about SUMXMY2 itself.
